title: Work & study
goal: Talk about your job and studies, and say what you can, may, must and don't have to do.
intro:
This unit adds three verb patterns that you will use constantly: **-గలను** (can, am able to), **-ఒచ్చు** (may, it's allowed / possible) and the negative **-లేను** (can't). Together with *-ఆలి* (must) from Unit 9, they let you talk about duties, permissions and abilities at work and school.

Note the job-talk question: Telugu speakers ask *మీరు ఏం చేస్తుంటారు?* ('what do you keep doing?').

vocab.note: Formal: ఉపాధ్యాయుడు; in school, children say సార్ / మేడం.
Understood: అర్థమైంది; didn't understand: అర్థం కాలేదు.

phrases.en: What do you do (for a living)?
There's a lot of work today.

grammar.title: Can and can't: -గల- and -లే-
grammar.body:
**Ability**: verb stem (in -a) + **గల-** + person ending:
చేయగలను (I can do) · చేయగలవు · చేయగలడు · చేయగలదు · చేయగలము · చేయగలరు

**Inability**: stem + **లే-** + ending:
చేయలేను (I can't) · చేయలేవు · చేయలేడు · చేయలేదు · చేయలేము · చేయలేరు
Careful: *చేయలేదు* can mean 'she/it can't do' or 'didn't do' (past negative, Unit 16); context decides.

For learned skills, the dative + **వచ్చు** (from Unit 2) is more natural: *నాకు ఈత వచ్చు* (I can swim), *నాకు డ్రైవింగ్ రాదు* (I can't drive).

examples.en: He can't do that job alone.

grammar.title: May, must, don't have to
grammar.body:
**May / it's okay to**: stem + **-ఒచ్చు** (-ochchu, written also -వచ్చు): *వెళ్ళొచ్చు* (you may go), *రావచ్చా?* (may I come in?). It also means 'might': *వర్షం పడొచ్చు* (it might rain).

**Must**: stem + **-ఆలి** (Unit 9): *పూర్తి చేయాలి* (I must finish).

**Don't have to**: infinitive + **-అక్కర్లేదు** (-akkarlēdu, 'no need'): *వెళ్ళక్కర్లేదు* (no need to go), *రానక్కర్లేదు* (no need to come).

**Must not**: stem + **-కూడదు**: *వాడకూడదు* (must not use).

examples.native: నేను ఈ రిపోర్టు ఈరోజే పూర్తి చేయాలి.
examples.roman: nēnu ī ripōrṭu īrōjē pūrti chēyāli.
examples.en: I have to finish this report today.
You don't have to come to the office tomorrow.
You must not use a phone in the exam.

dialogue.title: After Telugu class
dialogue.setting: Tom, a foreign student, stays behind to ask his Telugu teacher a question.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: కొంచెం కష్టంగా ఉంది మేడం. ఒక ప్రశ్న అడగొచ్చా?
lines.roman: konchem kaṣṭaṅgā undi mēḍam. oka prashna aḍagochchā?
lines.en: It's a bit difficult, madam. May I ask a question?

lines.speaker: Teacher
lines.native: చేయగలను అంటే నాకు శక్తి ఉంది. చేయొచ్చు అంటే అనుమతి ఉంది.
lines.roman: chēyagalanu aṇṭē nāku shakti undi. chēyochchu aṇṭē anumati undi.
lines.en: 'Chēyagalanu' means I have the ability. 'Chēyochchu' means there's permission.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.en: Got it. Can I read a Telugu newspaper?

lines.speaker: Teacher
lines.native: ఇంకా రెండు నెలలు ప్రాక్టీస్ చేయాలి. రోజూ కొంచెం చదవాలి.
lines.roman: iṅkā reṇḍu nelalu prākṭīs chēyāli. rōjū konchem chadavāli.
lines.en: You need two more months of practice. You must read a little every day.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: సరే మేడం, ప్రయత్నిస్తాను. రేపు క్లాసు ఉందా?
lines.roman: sarē mēḍam, prayatnistānu. rēpu klāsu undā?
lines.en: Okay, madam, I'll try. Is there class tomorrow?

lines.speaker: Teacher
lines.native: లేదు, రేపు సెలవు. రానక్కర్లేదు. కానీ హోంవర్కు పూర్తి చేయాలి!
lines.roman: lēdu, rēpu selavu. rānakkarlēdu. kānī hōmvarku pūrti chēyāli!
lines.en: No, tomorrow's a holiday. You needn't come. But you must finish your homework!

culture: Engineering and medicine carry enormous prestige, and the Telugu states send huge numbers of IT professionals abroad, especially to the USA, where Telugu is one of the fastest-growing languages. Students are coached intensively for entrance exams (EAMCET, JEE, NEET). Teachers are addressed as *సార్* and *మేడం* well into adult life, and a former teacher is always greeted with respect.

tip.title: I'm a teacher: నేను టీచర్ని
tip.body:
- 'I am a …' adds **-ని** to the job: నేను టీచర్**ని**, నేను నర్సు**ని**.
- For anyone else the job stands alone: మా అక్క **నర్సు**, మా నాన్న **రైతు**.
- A yes/no question adds **-ఆ**: మీరు ఇంజనీ**రా**?
- Ask about work with **మీరు ఏం చేస్తుంటారు?**
tip.pattern: నేను + job + ని · మా అక్క + job

sentences.en: I'm a teacher.
My elder sister is a nurse.
My father is a farmer.
Are you an engineer?
My brother's an engineer and I'm a nurse.

sentences.native: నేను ఒక పెద్ద కంపెనీలో ఉద్యోగం చేస్తున్నాను.
sentences.roman: nēnu oka pedda kampenīlō udyōgam chēstunnānu.
sentences.en: I work for a big company.
Where's your office?
What does your mother do?
I don't have a job.

tip.title: Have to, don't have to
tip.body:
- Must / have to: stem + **-ఆలి** (from Unit 9): పూర్తి **చేయాలి**, **వెళ్ళాలి**, **రావాలి**. Question: **చెప్పాలా?** 'should I tell?'
- No need to: infinitive + **-అక్కర్లేదు**: **వెళ్ళక్కర్లేదు** 'no need to go', **రానక్కర్లేదు** 'no need to come'.

sentences.en: I have to finish this work today.

sentences.native: పది గంటలకి మీటింగ్ ఉంది, తొందరగా వెళ్ళాలి.
sentences.roman: padi gaṇṭalaki mīṭiṅg undi, tondaragā veḷḷāli.
sentences.en: There's a meeting at ten, I have to get going.
I need to talk to the boss.
Should I tell the boss?
You have to come on Monday.
There's no meeting tomorrow, you don't need to come.
I don't have to go to the office on Saturday.
The salary isn't enough.
Do you need anything?
My colleague is a really nice guy.
My father runs a business.

lessons.title: Can you? I can, I can’t

tip.title: Can: -గల-, can't: -లే-
tip.body:
- Can: stem + **గల** + ending: రా**గల**ను 'I can come', చేయ**గల**రా? 'can you do it?'
- Can't: stem + **లే** + ending: రా**లే**ను 'I can't come', నడవ**లే**ను 'I can't walk'.
- For skills you've learned, dative + వచ్చు / రాదు sounds more natural: నాకు తెలుగు చదవడం వచ్చు.
tip.pattern: చేయ + గల + ను · చేయ + లే + ను

sentences.en: I can come tomorrow.
Can you finish this work today?
Sorry, I can't work on Sunday.
It's not hard, you can do it.
I can't walk that far.
Could you speak slowly?

sentences.native: నాకు తెలుగు చదవడం వచ్చు, రాయడం రాదు.
sentences.roman: nāku telugu chadavaḍam vachchu, rāyaḍam rādu.
sentences.en: I can read Telugu, but not write it.
It's really easy, give it a try.
I'll certainly try.

tip.title: May I? -ఒచ్చా?
tip.body:
- May / it's okay to: stem + **-ఒచ్చు** (also written -వచ్చు): **వెళ్ళొచ్చు** 'you may go', **కూర్చోవచ్చు** 'you can sit'.
- May I? add **-ఆ**: **రావచ్చా?** 'may I come in?', **వాడొచ్చా?** 'may I use it?'
- Don't mix it up with **-ఆలా?** 'must I?': వెళ్ళాలా? 'do I have to go?'

sentences.en: May I come in?
Can I go now?
You can sit here.
Could I learn Telugu from you?
The boss gave permission, I can go home.
May I use my phone?
I didn't understand, could you say it again?
Madam, what's the answer to this question?
My mum is teaching me Telugu.
I didn't understand this question.

tip.title: Mustn't: -కూడదు
tip.body:
- Must not: stem + **-కూడదు**: పరీక్షలో **మాట్లాడకూడదు** 'you mustn't talk in the exam'.
- Compare: **చదవాలి** 'must study' · **చదవొచ్చు** 'may study' · **చదవక్కర్లేదు** 'needn't study' · **చదవకూడదు** 'mustn't study'.

sentences.en: You mustn't talk in the exam.
You mustn't eat in class.
I have to study the lesson tonight.
The kids have to go to school at eight.
There's no school tomorrow, no need to get up early.
Students must study the lesson without fail.
My younger brother is at college.
What class are you in? (to a child)
Will the exam be hard?
